newsitem.title: USA: Dow jumps after reports allay inflation jitters.
newsitem.headline: Dow jumps after reports allay inflation jitters.

text.p: Stocks rallied Friday as investors breathed a sigh of relief after the government reported a modest rise in producer prices last month that helped calm inflation jitters on Wall Street.
The report also reassured bond investors, sending long-term interest rates lower for the first time this week and lending support to the stock market rally.

The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 45.10 points and stood at 5,966.77 just after 1 p.m. EDT. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a 14-8 margin on moderate New York Stock Exchange volume of about 249 million shares.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 5.60 points to 700.21 and the Nasdaq composite index, laden with high-technology stocks, added 8.75 points to 1,245.72.
Stocks and bonds had sold off steadily this week in the sessions ahead of Friday's producer price and retail sales reports.
The government reported that the Producer Price Index (PPI) rose 0.2 percent in September, slightly less than expected, in a sign that inflation remained tame at the wholesale level.

It also said retail sales rose 0.7 percent last month. While that was stronger than analysts had expected, sales rose a more modest 0.4 percent excluding strong new car sales. The government also sharply cut its estimate of August sales, to a 0.2 percent decline.
"On a two-month basis, the retail figures sort of washed out and the PPI tells us the status quo still stands," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
"It appears the bond market was pricing in potentially negative news and neither report gave us that," he said.
The bellwether 30-year Treasury rose 18/32, or $5.625 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield, which moves in the opposite direction from the price, to 6.84 percent from 6.89 percent on Thursday.
The 30-share Dow rose as much as 51 points, triggering the New York Stock Exchange's limits on programme trading.
Even with the welcome economic news, analysts said upcoming corporate earnings reports would likely hold the market in check for now.
"The market will probably stay in a range until we get a better feel for third quarter earnings reports," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.

Disappointing earnings news hurt several issues, notably drug maker Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc., which fell 5-1/8 to 36-3/8 after warning that quarterly earnings excluding charges would be about flat with the year-ago results. Analysts had expected earnings to rise about 20 percent.

Cascade Communications tumbled 10-3/8 to 76-1/8 despite announcing Thursday third quarter earnings above Wall Street forecasts. Analysts said the earnings did not far exceed those of the previous quarter, which hurt the stock.

"Cascade shows what happens when you're a momentum stock and you're in line with forecasts," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "If you're a momentum stock you have to do much better than be in line."
Shares in Sabre Group Holdings added 5-3/4 to 32-3/4 in their Wall Street debut. The unit of American Airlines parent AMR Corp. owns the Sabre travel reservation system.

Paracelsus Healthcare tumbled 5-1/8 to 5 in the first trading in the company's shares since it warned Wednesday night of weak third quarter earnings. The company also said it may restate earnings for the last three quarters.
The American Stock Exchange index was off 0.60 at 579.39.
